Across three observational studies examining caregiver-assisted HIV testing using an HIV self-testing (HIVST) kit, no physical harm to children was reported. In two of these studies, no physical harm to caregivers as a result of the intervention was reported. However, 4% (9 out of 2250) of caregivers reported adverse events affecting children, including six cases of gum pain, three cases of gum bleeding, and one case of itching. The evidence was rated as very low certainty due to critical concerns. 7. The evidence was critically and seriously biased due to several factors: (1) confounding factors, such as gender imbalance, across all three studies; (2) participant selection in two studies, where caregivers were pre-screened for intimate partner violence prior to the intervention, resulting in 53% (226 caregivers) being screened out; (3) significant cross-arm switches in one study; (4) missing data in one study, which had a 27% attrition rate; and (5) measurement of outcomes, which was critically dependent on self-reporting across all three studies. It is important to note that the denominator used in the analysis is not based on an ITT approach but rather on the number of individuals interviewed.
